user_query: My employer hasn't paid my salary for 3 months. What can I do?
variations: Boss owes me salary. Where do I report?
How do I claim unpaid wages?
Company never pay me three months already
Who do I complain to if I don't get paid?
part_a_general_info: Under the Employment Act 1968, employers must pay salary within 7 days after the end of each salary period. If your employer has not paid, you may file a salary claim with the Tripartite Alliance for Dispute Management (TADM). Claims must generally be filed within 1 year from the date salary was due. If you have left the company, you must file within 6 months of your last day. The Employment Claims Tribunals (ECT) can hear claims up to $20,000 (or $30,000 with union assistance). Mediation at TADM is mandatory before ECT.
triage_questions: Q1: Are you still working for the employer, or have you left?
Q2: When was the last salary payment you received?
Q3: How much salary is owed in total?
Q4: Are you a Singapore Citizen, PR, or on a work permit?
Q5: Have you already filed a claim with TADM?
branching_logic: If Q1 = 'left' → Check if within 6-month limitation. If outside, flag as time-barred and escalate.
If Q4 = 'work permit' → Additionally inform about MOM regulations.
If Q5 = 'already filed TADM' → Branch to ECT pathway.
routing: Route A (No TADM claim): Refer to TADM for mandatory mediation. Provide filing link and limitation period.
Route B (TADM failed): If Claim Referral Certificate obtained, refer to ECT. Refer to PBSG employment clinic if needed.
Route C (Work permit holder): Additionally refer to MOM. Escalate to PBSG staff for specialist referral.
Route D (Time-barred): Inform claim may be time-barred. Escalate to PBSG staff to assess exceptions.
guardrail: Must NOT advise on specific contractual entitlements or draft any letter of demand. General statutory framework and routing only.
